facts.text: Chattanooga Valley was founded in 1839, but its roots trace back to 1816 when brothers John and Lewis Ross opened Ross’s Landing with a trading post and ferry.
The name “Chattanooga” comes from a Muskogean word meaning “rock coming to a point.”.
Chattanooga Valley sits within the Chattanooga, TN–GA Metropolitan Statistical Area, linking it to a larger regional community.
A digital treasure trove called Deep Zoom Chattanooga lets residents and visitors explore rare historic photos in high resolution.
Sam Hall, creator of ChattanoogaHistory.com, received a Tennessee Historical Commission Certificate of Merit for preserving digital images of the city’s past.
The valley’s history spans settlement, war, boom, decline, and renaissance, reflecting the broader story of the region.
